          Aston Villa vs Man City Prediction: Premier League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 22, 2026
          
                      Dan Edwards / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to Saturday’s early Premier League kick-off at Villa Park with our Aston Villa vs Man City prediction and preview.

Manchester City are aiming to become just the eighth team in English top-flight history to start a league campaign with eight consecutive wins, but face a stern test against a resurgent Aston Villa side.

Chelsea, who won their first nine games in 2005-06, and Liverpool, who won their first eight games in 2019-20, are the only teams to better City’s start to the current campaign under Enzo Maresca. Both teams went on to lift the title in their respective seasons.

But – separate to all of the goings-on off the field – City are still not regarded as favourites to win the Premier League this season by the Opta supercomputer. Arsenal lead the way with a 47.7% chance of going back-to-back, with City close behind at 39.9% at the time of writing.
While the points have been rolling in, even the clubs’ own fans would admit the performances haven’t been quite as assured as the league table suggests.

According to Opta's expected points table, City are currently the Premier League’s biggest overperformers, with nearly eight points more (21) than expected (13.2) based on the quality of chances for and against in their games.

One-sided defeats against Arsenal in the Community Shield and Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Champions League may be more representative of the club’s genuine current level compared to best-in-class opposition.
Could this season bear some similarity to the 2016-17 campaign, when City opened with six straight wins under new manager Pep Guardiola, before ultimately finishing in third place?

Maresca will aim to prove otherwise, but a trip to Villa Park to face an in-form Aston Villa team is represents of his toughest tasks so far as City boss. Villa are better, and have much more quality, than their current position of 12th suggests.

After winning just one of their first five games in all competitions this season as Unai Emery’s dressing room came to grips with losing a handful of their best players, Villa have recovered with five wins from their next six.
Central to their improved performance levels have been summer imports Nicolas Jackson and Johan Manzambi, who have scored eight goals combined in all competitions since the second week of September.

Alas, Manzambi – who has scored or assisted in all three of the games he has started in the Premier League – missed the club’s midweek UEFA Champions League victory against Viking through injury and is considered a doubt for the visit of City.
Should he be deemed fit enough to start, he could become the first Aston Villa player to register a goal or assist in each of their first Premier League starts.

Manzambi is one of a number of injury concerns for Emery. Villa are currently struggling to field a left-back; Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Matteo Ruggeri are both out, while Ian Maatsen may not be fit enough to start.

City aren’t without injury concerns of their own. Erling Haaland hobbled off the pitch against Ipswich last week and was an unused substitute against AEK Athens in midweek. A hat-trick from Phil Foden meant City coped just fine without their leading man, but their ability to do so against Premier League opposition is another question.

As well as having the most goals (8), Haaland has had the most shots (27) and shots on target (13) of any player in the Premier League this season, while he ranks second for big chances (12) and touches in the opposition box (40).
Haaland’s potential absence may be the biggest threat to City’s 100% winning start.
Aston Villa have won four of their last six Premier League games against Manchester City, as many as in their previous 35 against them (D5 L26).
Man City have lost their last two league games against Aston Villa, last losing three in a row to them between August 1962 and September 1966.
Man City made it eight wins from eight games in 43.0% of simulations. The next-most common result was a home victory for Villa, at 31.6%, while the game was drawn in 25.3% of sims.
